title: Noble Sissle's society orchestra and the Shuffle Along connection
summary: Moore describes Sissle's eighteen-piece band, Flournoy Miller, and Sissle's songs with Eubie Blake.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: With Noble Sissle, he played a lot of cotillions and his was more a kind of society orchestra, I guess, how large was it at that time?
Yeh, Noble was -- you mean how big the band was?
He had a full band, and in the band of about 18 men he had Flournay Miller -- Miller and Lyle --

They all worked with the Shuffle Along with Eubie Blake.

Yeah. Flournay Miller's daughter played the harp and when they opened up the theme song was "I'm Just Wild About Harry" and it was the best band even with Noble, because he had the name internationally.
London. New York's Diamond Horseshoe, pretty well known, and it was an experience to be with Noble.
He sang with that band of his, didn't he?

Noble was singing a thing called "Love Will Find a Way," and he was singing that, and he would stand up in front in the theater with a piece of sheet music. Now, you're a performer you're not supposed to be reading and looking at the lyrics, you know, you're supposed to know the lyrics. But I think he figured his name was big enough to say, I don't care, I'm going to sing it with this when I don't know all the words. So he used to perform like that, "Love Will Find a Way." And you know, he collaborated with Eubie Blake. I think he wrote the lyrics to "Wild about Harry" as well as "Love Will Find a Way."

It was quite an experience knowing that Noble was in this Shuffle Along thing with Eubie Blake, years gone back during the Twenties, I think. I think that was around the late '20s.
That's the show they had Josephine Baker, wasn't it? I think she was in Shuffle Along, too.
I don't believe she was, we can check on that but there were a number of other musicians and composers who were involved in that orchestra. There was William Grant Still.
In a show like Shuffle Along, the names would come along and they would leave the show and go on --
